headline: Okanagan Provincial Park Camping and Boating Access
reservation: While day-use access to public beaches is generally open, overnight stays at Okanagan Lake Provincial Park or Bear Creek require seasonal booking through BC Parks. High summer demand often leads to fully booked campsites months in advance; always verify current booking windows and available services on the official portal before arrival.

days.title: Central Vineyards and Lakeside Vistas

stops.name: Knox Mountain Park
stops.detail: Drive or hike to the Apex Lookout for an expansive view of the lake's central basin and the floating bridge.

stops.name: Mission Creek Greenway
stops.detail: Walk the scenic lower trails that follow the creek toward the lake's eastern shore.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for local Kelowna transit; conditions vary with summer traffic.
days.note: Parking at popular trailheads fills early during the July heat.

days.title: Southern Naramata Bench and Bluffs

stops.name: Munson Mountain
stops.detail: View the iconic 'Penticton' sign and look northward across the full length of the lake.

stops.name: Naramata Creek Falls
stops.detail: Follow the trail through the canyon to see the cooling falls just inland from the lakeshore.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours for the winding road along the Naramata Bench; conditions vary.
days.note: The Naramata Road is narrow and frequented by cyclists; exercise caution on curves.

days.title: Northern Bays and Provincial Shorelines

stops.name: Kalamalka Lake Provincial Park
stops.detail: Explore the distinct turquoise waters and ridge trails that separate the two major valley lakes.

stops.name: Ellison Provincial Park
stops.detail: Access the unique granite headlands and small coves perfect for shore-based exploration.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 hours for travel between Vernon and northern park gates; conditions vary.
days.note: State of water quality can fluctuate; check for local beach advisories before swimming.

intel.title: Urban Beach Lots
intel.text: City-managed lots in Kelowna use digital payment systems; spaces near City Park are highly contested during weekends. Smaller provincial lots north of the city may have limited capacity for oversized vehicles.

intel.title: Highland Dead Zones
intel.text: While urban centers have robust coverage, signal strength drops significantly when driving the Westside Road or high-elevation lookouts. Download offline maps if exploring the forested ridges overlooking the water.

intel.title: Corridor Services
intel.text: Fuel is readily available along Highway 97 connecting the main cities. If heading into the high backcountry plateaus, ensure tanks are filled in the valley floor.

intel.title: Summer Peak Heat
intel.text: Mid-day temperatures in the Okanagan often exceed 30°C in July and August. Plan strenuous hikes for early morning to avoid the peak solar intensity.

intel.title: Waterway Navigation
intel.text: Public boat launches are located in all three gateway cities, but some may have seasonal depth restrictions. Always check for invasive species inspection requirements before launching private watercraft.

plan.arrival: Collect your vehicle at Kelowna International Airport (YLW) and head south for 20 minutes to stock up on supplies in downtown Kelowna before checking into lakeside rentals.
plan.vehicle: Standard cars are suitable for the main highway; consider a 4WD if accessing remote forest service roads on the lake's west side.
plan.goldenHour: Sunset from the Westside Road overlooks offers a glow over the vineyards of the Mission District, varying by season.
